mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in PARKS from near-flat to roughly baseline signals a broader easing of leisure movement that will spill into nearby discretionary shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -22.0 at t-1w to -0.1 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved from -42.0 to -36.3
failure_condition: If PARKS remains near zero or higher but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean within 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, residents substitute local errands for commuting-linked shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks while TRANSIT is persistently negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its recent 4-week mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT above the recent low signals relaxation of mobility frictions; retail activity follows with a lag, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a negative level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -36.0 at t-1w to -33.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 28-day mean over the subsequent 28 days, the signal fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid move in PARKS toward zero during spring indicates stronger outdoor seasonal demand, which diverts some weekend traffic into shopping corridors and raises RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below -10 to above -5 within one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS shifted from -30.3 at t-2w to -0.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS crosses the stated threshold but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 7 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT means more everyday trips are resuming, and that broad recovery converts into higher discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both improve for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week average, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in WORKPLACES reduces weekday foot traffic and lunch-hour spillovers to retail, so RETAIL_REC will stay lower over the next two weeks unless work mobility rebounds.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains around -33 to -35 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains deeply negative but RETAIL_REC rises above its recent mean within two weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If residential staying-in is no longer increasing while transit remains below baseline, the city is in a partial-return regime where discretionary shopping still lags, leaving RETAIL_REC flat to lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 1 point week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -30
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from 8.6 to 7.4 while TRANSIT stayed near -33
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL eases and TRANSIT stays below -30 but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a near-baseline PARKS reading and improving GROCERY_PHARM indicates a broader seasonal normalization in errands and outings, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is near zero while GROCERY_PHARM improved from -28.4 to -24.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays near baseline and GROCERY_PHARM continues improving but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the mechanism fails.
